name: sol_ll_2
description: Custom low-level function dispatcher lacks revert on unmatched selector, allowing fallthrough into unintended bytecode
question: The source file in `source` implements a custom low-level function dispatcher (e.g. inline assembly comparing calldata selectors against known function signatures) that, after comparing the calldata selector against all supported function signatures and fallback conditions without finding a match, allows execution to continue into subsequent code or bytecode instead of explicitly reverting or stopping, excluding dispatchers that end every non-matching branch with revert, stop, or return.
criteria: Assembly dispatcher chain checks calldataload selector against multiple function signatures with switch/if-else, and the final else branch falls through to subsequent code instead of calling revert(0,0)
A fallback-style dispatcher in raw bytecode/assembly compares selectors sequentially but omits a terminating revert after the last comparison, letting execution proceed into whatever bytecode follows
Custom proxy or multiplexer contract written in assembly matches known selectors but has no default case that reverts, so unmatched calls execute unintended jump destinations
